summary: @servicetitan/lazy-module preinstall drops Bun runtime and executes obfuscated bundled payload
details: package.json declares preinstall="node setup.mjs". setup.mjs is identifier-obfuscated (obfuscator.io-style _0xXXXX names with mapping-object dispatch) and downloads the Bun runtime from github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases at install time, then invokes execFileSync(bun, [math_init.js]). math_init.js is a 727KB bun-cjs bundle whose header is "// @bun @bun-cjs" followed by a shuffled string-array constructor (WV8StW) and a large numeric/character map that reconstructs URLs, paths, and API calls at runtime, hiding all destinations from static inspection. The package's advertised purpose is a React Suspense lazy-module helper (dist/index.js is a small React wrapper referencing homepage https://docs.st.dev/ and repo servicetitan/uikit), which has no legitimate need to fetch a second language runtime or to execute a bundled obfuscated binary at install. The obfuscated payload and preinstall script do not exist in the upstream servicetitan/uikit repository, consistent with a maintainer-account compromise or name-hijack republish that grafts an alternate-runtime dropper onto a legitimate-looking library. On every npm install this fires automatically and runs attacker-controlled Bun-compiled code with the installer's privileges.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
